clue.text: Horse has to strike, losing lead

parts.note: has to means must

indicators.note: losing its lead means the word for strike drops its first letter

parts.note: to strike is to bang

explanation.surface: A horse that must hit out, having slipped its lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing lead' takes the B off BANG, leaving ANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a wild or half-wild horse of the American plains.

clue.text: French writer is longer penning story

indicators.note: penning means the word for longer encloses the word for story

parts.note: more, as in more time, means longer
a story can be a lie, as in telling stories

explanation.surface: A French author is said to be taking more time writing his tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the seventeenth-century French playwright of Tartuffe and The Misanthrope.

clue.text: Hounds me and others like me!

definitions.meaning: breeds of gun dog, such as the Irish and English
the speaker is the compiler, so crossword compilers in general

explanation.surface: The compiler cheekily calls themself and their colleagues dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Setters are both gun dogs and the people who compile crosswords.

clue.text: Let everybody almost get into debt

parts.note: all means everybody

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to owe money is to be in debt

explanation.surface: Permitting everyone to come close to borrowing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' takes the last letter off OWE, leaving OW.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow is to let or permit.

clue.text: Sprout fur around a time after midnight

indicators.note: after puts the fur and its contents behind the midnight letter

parts.note: the middle letter of the word night

indicators.note: around means the fur word goes round the article and the time letter

parts.note: ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat

explanation.surface: Fur growing at some hour past midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is a crossword favourite for G, the middle letter of NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: To germinate is to begin to grow, as a seed sprouts.

clue.text: Soaps following end of Scrubs including Hospital

indicators.note: including means the word for following takes the hospital letter inside it

parts.note: following, as in coming afterwards, means later
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Television soap operas airing after the medical show Scrubs, with hospital settings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to soap is to lather, so lathers fits 'soaps' in the third person.

clue.text: Misses reportedly loose

indicators.note: reportedly says it is how the word sounds when heard

parts.note: lax means loose or slack

explanation.surface: Young women are said to be of easy virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: To lack something is to be without it, as one misses something absent.

clue.text: Excel scan modified in course

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the word for course

parts.note: a trend is a general course or direction

indicators.note: modified means the letters of scan are altered in order

explanation.surface: Instructions to change a spreadsheet scan during a training course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' turns SCAN into ANSC, which goes 'in' TREND.
explanation.definitionFit: To transcend is to surpass or go beyond, as to excel does.

clue.text: Ecstasy consequently found in endless modern rave

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: found in means the word for consequently sits inside the trimmed word
endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: new means modern
thus means consequently or therefore

explanation.surface: Drugs turn up at a contemporary dance party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts NEW to NE, which THUS is 'found in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rave is to talk with great enthusiasm, the same as to enthuse.

clue.text: Better drink, consuming last of lager before idiot

indicators.note: before places the first part ahead of the idiot word
consuming means the drink word swallows the letter

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the next word

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Drinking the dregs of lager ahead of a fool is a superior choice.
explanation.definitionFit: To better something is to improve on or surpass it.

clue.text: More insignificant rubbish about Latin…

indicators.note: about means the word for rubbish goes around the Latin abbreviation

parts.note: rubbish strewn about is litter

explanation.surface: Dismissing a classical language as trivial junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Littler is a comparative of little, meaning smaller or of less importance.

clue.text: …more relevant subsequent to Church Synod perhaps

indicators.note: subsequent to places the word for more relevant after the church abbreviation

parts.note: apter is the comparative of apt, meaning more fitting

explanation.surface: Something judged more pertinent than a meeting of the Church's governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapter is an assembly of the canons of a cathedral, an example of a church governing body like a synod.

clue.text: Plant seeds while ignoring hard ground

indicators.note: ground, as in milled into pieces, signals the letters are rearranged
ignoring says the hard abbreviation is left out of the word while

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Sowing seeds while avoiding difficult soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring hard' drops the H from WHILE to leave WILE; 'ground' then shuffles SEEDS and WILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is an Alpine flowering plant with woolly white bracts.

clue.text: Accordingly American embraces American composer

indicators.note: embraces means the first pieces wrap around the second American

parts.note: accordingly means so, as in therefore
US is an abbreviation for American, as in US citizen
US is an abbreviation for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: An American hugging a fellow American, introduced as an American composer.
explanation.definitionFit: John Philip Sousa was the composer of marches such as The Stars and Stripes Forever.

clue.text: Stand in position for painter?

parts.note: reads like a model posing for an artist, but describes the stand that holds a canvas in place for a painter

explanation.surface: An instruction to a sitter to hold still for a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame that supports an artist's canvas while they work.

clue.text: View Loch Ness catching also head of serpent

indicators.note: catching means the outer pieces enclose the inner ones

parts.note: L is a map abbreviation for loch or lake
a ness is a headland or cape
and means also

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A view of Loch Ness that also catches a glimpse of the monster's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Ness is a Scottish lake famed for its supposed monster; here 'Ness' is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is an expanse of scenery, a view of the countryside.

clue.text: Understanding unusually seen as comprising conflict

indicators.note: comprising means the rearranged letters contain the word for conflict
unusually means the letters of seen as appear in an unusual order

parts.note: war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: Grasp of a situation that, unusually, is regarded as involving strife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' turns SEEN AS into AENESS, which 'comprising' wraps around WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Awareness is knowledge or perception of a situation, a synonym of understanding.

clue.text: Range enclosing peak over in Australia perhaps

indicators.note: enclosing means the range word goes around the next pieces

parts.note: the Andes are a South American mountain range
a tip is a peak or top
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A mountain chain surrounding a summit somewhere down under.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antipodes are the lands on the opposite side of the globe from Britain, Australia being an example.

clue.text: Clean scent if I'd showered?

indicators.note: showered, as in scattered about, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Would washing get rid of a smell?
explanation.definitionFit: To disinfect is to clean something of germs with chemicals.

clue.text: Cryptic, if edited, shows up deficiency

indicators.note: in a down entry, up says the letters are read from bottom to top
shows means the clue words display the letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A crossword clue, once edited, reveals a shortcoming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' reveals TICIFED in 'crypTIC, IF EDited' and 'up', in a down entry, reads it upwards. 'Cryptic' poses as a description, not fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is a shortfall or deficiency, especially of money.

clue.text: Lust ends in transparent cover

indicators.note: in means those letters go inside the word for transparent

parts.note: sheer means so thin as to be see-through

indicators.note: ends picks the first and last letters of the word lust

explanation.surface: Desire visible through see-through clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' gives LT from Lust, which goes 'in' SHEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelter is protection or cover from weather or danger.

clue.text: Small crucifix over more than one entrance

indicators.note: over says the combined pieces are turned around

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a rood is a crucifix, especially one above a church screen

explanation.surface: A little cross hanging above several doorways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SROOD round as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Doors are entrances, plural to match 'more than one'.

clue.text: Beaten due to no pants!

indicators.note: pants, British slang for rubbish, signals the letters are rearranged badly

explanation.surface: Defeated because someone forgot their underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for poor or rubbish, here the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outdone is to be beaten or surpassed by someone else.

clue.text: Not spending money to catch Queen? Tough!

indicators.note: to catch means the miserly word traps the queen's letter inside

parts.note: stingy means mean, reluctant to spend
R, for Regina, is the usual abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A miser trying to snare the monarch finds it hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringy meat is tough and fibrous.

clue.text: Fondles female in front of slippery customers

indicators.note: in front of places the female letter before the slippery creatures

parts.note: eels are proverbially slippery

explanation.surface: Groping a woman ahead of some shifty characters.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel someone can mean to touch or caress them, as fondles does.

clue.text: Fan is 'matchless' without Liverpool, say…

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for matchless goes around the port

parts.note: matchless means super, beyond compare
Liverpool is an example of a port

explanation.surface: A football follower says his team is unbeatable without Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', a convention that misleads because it usually means 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan of a team is a supporter of it.

clue.text: Stickiness with exercise and training initially

definitions.text: Stickiness with exercise and training initially

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Sticky skin is what comes from exertion and workouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweat is the moisture the skin gives off during exercise, making it sticky.

clue.text: State of the old lady in a house turned upside-down

indicators.note: in means the mother word goes inside the turned pieces
in a down entry, upside-down means read from bottom to top

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, one's old lady

explanation.surface: Asking about the condition of a mother in a topsy-turvy home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned upside-down' reverses A HO to OHA, and MA goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city of Nebraska; the setter loosely takes it for a US state.

clue.text: …Villa's excessive in enclosure

definitions.note: the possessive here is read as villa is, with the following words giving the wordplay

indicators.note: in means the word for excessive sits inside the word for enclosure

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure
OTT, short for over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: Continuing the football theme, Aston Villa are said to be over the top within their ground.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is British shorthand for 'over the top', meaning excessive. The ellipsis links this to the previous clue's football picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa and a cottage are both kinds of country house, the one grander than the other.

clue.text: Force to continue slowly round job centre

indicators.note: round means the phrase for continue slowly goes around the middle letter

parts.note: to drag on is to continue tediously slowly

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of the word job

explanation.surface: Pushing on at a crawl past the unemployment office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'job centre' looks like the British unemployment office, but gives only the O at the middle of JOB.
explanation.definitionFit: To dragoon someone is to coerce or force them into doing something.

clue.text: In discomfort or mental anguish

indicators.note: In signals that the answer is found within the following words

explanation.surface: Describing distress that is either physical or mental.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe suffering, a synonym of anguish.

clue.text: State drawn into secretive work in captivity

indicators.note: drawn into means the word for state is pulled inside the word for secretive

parts.note: sly means secretive or furtive
to aver is to state or assert

explanation.surface: A nation pulled into covert operations while held prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavery is forced labour by people held as property, or more loosely drudgery.
